newsitem.title: USA: CME hog, pork belly futures finish lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog, pork belly futures finish lower.

text.p: Losses were pared in CME hog futures late but values closed lower on further weakness in cash hog prices, traders said. Pork belly futures remained pressured by sliding cash belly prices.

Expectations for steady to lower cash hog markets again Tuesday weighed on hog futures but losses were reduced by ideas cash prices may strengthen later this week. Packers have adequate animals on hand after they cut the kill rate over the weekend, traders said.
Also, wet fields will keep farmers from harvesting briefly early this week and allow time to market hogs, they said.

However, drier conditions were seen later in the week which will likely tighten marketings. The reduced hog slaughter pace will also firm up pork product prices and improve packer margins, sources said.
October also was underpinned by expectations there will be no delivery notices posted Monday, first notice day.
Locals and scattered commission houses sold October early while Refco, Merrill Lynch and Rosenthal Collins sold December. Rand Financials was a light buyer of December, pit sources said.
In hog options, trading was slow, even with single strikes available for trading in February. Volatility was steady, pit sources said.

Pork bellies showed carryover pressure from the start linked to the weak tone in cash bellies which were quoted generally $2 per cwt lower at noon. Cash values were seen falling further despite reduced slaughter, traders said.

Cash sources noted that September is one of the last strong demand months for bacon and interest drops off quickly going into the fall. Also, recent high cash prices cut off retail interest, they said.
The reduced pace of hog slaughter kept futures prices from tumbling in generally slow dealings, they added.
LFG, Lind-Waldock, LIT division of First Options and Cargill Investor Services sold during the day, traders said. Prudential and ING bought early.

Hog futures closed 0.325 cent a lb lower to 0.100 higher with only distant December up and nearby December off most at 57.475 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.925 to 0.850 cent a lb lower for traded months with February off 0.900 at 76.150 cents.
